_note: Core English dictionary for the understanding module (memory/researcher/understanding.py). Format: term -> [definition, usage]. Definitions <=12 words. Sibling: dictionary_project.json. Pointer: memory/INDEX.md.
memory: stored information kept for later use
the agent keeps project memory in files
recall: bring stored information back into mind or context
recall the last decision before answering
remember: keep something in mind; store for later
remember to commit after each change
context: surrounding information that gives meaning to a request
prompt: the user's current instruction to the model
extract key terms from every prompt
reply: a response given back to the asker
post the reply, then run recall
model: an AI system that processes text and predicts
pick a smaller model for background tasks
agent: a program that acts on behalf of a user
the agent reads memory before acting
module: a self-contained unit of code in one file
import the understanding module at startup
function: a named block of code that takes inputs and returns output
call the lookup function with the term
variable: a named value that can change during a run
store the result in a variable
loop: repeating a set of steps until a condition ends it
loop over each key term in turn
error: something going wrong; a failure signal from code
log the error and degrade gracefully
bug: an unintended flaw in code causing wrong behavior
test: a check that verifies code behaves as expected
run the test suite after each patch
commit: save a snapshot of changes into version control
commit the dictionary files with a short message
branch: a parallel line of development in a repo
work on a branch, then merge
merge: combine two lines of development into one
merge the feature once tests pass
patch: a small set of changes applied to existing code
apply the patch script, check its markers
anchor: an exact text snippet used to locate a change point
splice new code before the anchor line
index: a lookup structure mapping keys to locations or values
build an index of memory files by term
pointer: a reference that says where something else lives
INDEX.md holds pointers to every memory module
file: a named block of data stored on disk
write the result to a json file
folder: keep researcher notes in one folder
path: the address of a file or folder on disk
use relative paths from the project root
line: one row of text in a file
replace only the target line, not neighbors
code: instructions written for a computer to execute
read the code before changing it
script: a short program run directly, often one-off
run the patch script from the terminal
execute: run code so its instructions take effect
execute the tool call in order
build: assemble or create something from parts
build pre-context before sending the prompt
fix: repair something that is broken or wrong
verify: check that something is true or correct
verify the file exists before reading it
confirm: state that something has been checked and is so
confirm the test passed before moving on
check: look at something to see if it is right
log: a running record of events, written in order
append each step to the run log
state: the current condition or values of a system
read the goal state from the ledger
status: a short report on how something is going
post status only when it changes
goal: a desired outcome the work is aimed at
keep main goals moving without holdups
task: a unit of work to be done
queue the task in the background list
queue: an ordered list of items waiting for processing
long probes go to the background queue
blocker: something that prevents progress until resolved
list every blocker, then clear them one by one
stall: progress stopping even though work should continue
a stalled goal needs a nudge or re-plan
change: record each change with a commit
update: update the index after adding files
add: include something that was not there before
add the new term to the dictionary
remove: take something out so it is no longer present
remove stale entries from the log
delete: delete only after a backup exists
create: make something that did not exist before
create the data file with sample entries
write: produce text or data into a file or field
write results as json, one record per line
read: take in text or data to use it
read the last twenty prompts for gaps
send: transmit something from here to somewhere else
send the pre-context with the main prompt
receive: receive the tool result before continuing
message: a unit of communication between people or systems
each chat message becomes one agent turn
chat: an ongoing conversation, here between user and agents
user: the person giving instructions and receiving results
ask the user before buying or deleting
tool: a capability an agent can call to act
use a tool when it materially improves the answer
call: one use of a function or tool with its arguments
batch independent calls into one block
result: the output produced by running something
keep results minimal to save context
output: what a program or model produces
cap the output length for long files
input: what is given to a program or model to process
clean the input before keying terms
data: facts and values stored for later processing
load the data file once at startup
record: one entry in a structured collection of entries
append one record per completed task
note: a short written reminder or observation
leave a note explaining the decision
plan: an ordered set of steps toward a goal
work the plan in small parts
step: one action within a larger sequence
take one step, then check the screen
limit: the maximum allowed amount of something
budget: an allowance of a resource, here tokens or time
spend the output budget on code, not prose
token: one unit of text a model counts against its budget
shorter replies leave more tokens for tools
